verdict.rationale: Both refactors preserve observable behavior. Change A's reordering of tax and coupon lookup is safe because `tax_rate` never raises, and its release of `order.items` on a declined payment matches the original `reserved` list at that point. A also adds characterization tests, which it ran against the unchanged code, covering the pricing, rollback and receipt paths the original suite missed. That is what makes a no-behavior-change refactor of production code safe to merge. B adds no tests, exposes all its helpers as public module functions, and its report contains inaccurate claims.
a_issues: Pricing now computes the discount, including the coupon validation, before tax. This is harmless only because `tax_rate` cannot raise, and the report does not note the reordering.
`_charge` releases `order.items` instead of the list of actually reserved items. This is equivalent today but couples correctness to the earlier step having reserved everything.
The tax loop now runs separately from the subtotal sum, so line totals are computed twice.
b_issues: No new tests, even though the existing 9 tests leave the VIP discount, shipping threshold, rounding, coupon errors and partial rollback unprotected.
Helpers are public names without a leading underscore (`validate_order`, `compute_discount`, etc.), which needlessly widens the module's API.
The report wrongly claims an unknown country 'fails' before an invalid coupon; `tax_rate` falls back to a default and never raises.
The report suggests `list[OrderItem] if you have that model`, but `shop.models.Item` exists; the type hints are a loose `list`.
`charge_customer` takes six parameters, including the threaded-through `reserved` list.

verdict.rationale: Both refactors keep production behavior. A is the more literal move of the existing code. B first added 18 characterization tests and ran them against the unchanged code. Those tests pin down the pricing, rounding, threshold and rollback behavior that the original 9 tests left unprotected, which is what a no-behavior-change refactor of live checkout code needs. B's small reorderings (tax_rate called after the coupon check, releasing order.items instead of the reserved list) are not observable with valid inputs, though A preserves the original order more strictly.
a_issues: Adds no tests, so the refactor of pricing and rollback paths is checked only by the 9 existing tests, which miss VIP discount, the shipping threshold, per-line rounding, partial rollback and receipt failure.
The helpers are public, module-level names, which grows the module's API surface without need.
`charge_customer` takes a loosely typed `reserved: list` parameter only so it can release stock.
The report suggests tightening the type to `list[OrderItem]`, but the repository's model is `Item`, so the advice is inaccurate.
b_issues: `_price_order` now calls `_tax_cents` (and so `tax_rate`) after the coupon check, which subtly reorders evaluation compared with the original (not observable with valid string country codes).
`_charge` releases `order.items` instead of the list of reserved items. That is equivalent only because reservation fully succeeded, so it is an implicit coupling.
Did not run a type checker or linter (stated in the report).
